content.title: Leyden Road Improvements
content.summary: The Leyden Road improvements project will widen and repave Leyden Road from Indiana Street to Highway 93, enhancing bike and pedestrian safety by adding bike lanes, sidewalks, and other roadway features. Funded primarily through Traffic Impact Fees from the Leyden Rock development, the project is currently in the design phase, with construction expected to take about one year once it begins. Additionally, the city is evaluating alternative evacuation routes for the Leyden neighborhood, which will improve emergency evacuation times significantly.
content.body:
## Overview

The Leyden Road improvements project will widen and repave Leyden Road (W 82nd Ave) from Indiana Street to Highway 93. This project will enhance bike and pedestrian safety along the corridor. Improvements include adding:

- bike lanes,
- sidewalks,
- roadway repaving,
- curb and gutter, and
- in some areas wider travel lanes or medians.

This project is funded through the Traffic Impact Fees from the Leyden Rock development. Additional funding may be needed to complete construction.

## Project Area

![map highlighting road work area on 82nd avenue between Indiana and highway 93](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4775)

Bike lanes, curb and gutter, medians, and sidewalks will be installed from Indiana to Orion Way. Repaving will occur from Indiana to Culebra St.

## Timeline

The project is currently under design. Design plans, including engineering studies, are being coordinated with CDOT and Jefferson County. The construction timeline is still being determined based on funding and design approvals. Once work begins construction is anticipated to take approximately one year to complete.

### Updates

Updated 6/4/26

- **Ongoing:**design
- **Complete:**design consultant selected; Leyden Creek at 82nd Ave. drainage study; Environmental and preliminary geotechnical studies; Traffic counts and classifications; Preliminary survey and investigation.

## Evacuation Route Alternatives Analysis

### Current Update

Updated 6/4/26

The City team is moving forward with the design and construction of the west emergency route detailed below. Construction may begin as soon as late 2026 or 2027. The timeline is dependent on agreements with partner agencies and subject to change.

### Overview

The City evaluated potential alternative evacuation routes from the Leyden neighborhood based on concerns about evacuation constraints. The City analyzed several potential improvements for the neighborhood. This analysis looked at engineering feasibility, property impacts, costs, and complexity.

**Evacuation routes will vary based on the emergency.** Some routes may be closed. Always listen to emergency personnel and follow directions on site.

### Evacuation time, cost, and schedule assumptions

Evacuation status changes are rough estimations, based on simulated modeling. This looks at the effects an option may have on total neighborhood evacuation time. Different parts of the neighborhood may benefit more or less from a given alternative. The costs and schedules for these routes are preliminary and high-level projections used for concept planning and scoping.

### Leyden Road Project

The Leyden Road improvements (above) will significantly help with the ability to effectively evacuate the neighborhood. The widening will allow the road to be reconfigured to two lanes out and one lane in during an emergency evacuation. This work was identified as a priority from the Leyden Emergency Preparedness Study completed by the City in 2024.

- **Evacuation status change:** High - more than 1 to 1.5 hour reduction in overall neighborhood evacuation time.
- **Requirements:**annexation, ROW acquisition, complex grading with retaining walls, utility improvements, streetscape improvements including widening, curb and gutter
- **Estimated cost:** $10-20 million
- **Timeline:** 2-5 Years to Construction Complete
- **Cost Benefit:**High

### West Emergency Route (under design)

- **Route:**Westbound via Gore Street through landfill service road to Highway 93
- **Evacuation status change:**Medium - 30 to 45 minute reduction in overall neighborhood evacuation time; improvement concentrated in western neighborhoods.
- **Requirements:** Remove guardrail, construct 14’ gravel road, new landfill gates/fence, access easements and construction variables, maintenance plan
- **Estimated cost:** $500,000 - $1.5 million
- **Timeline:**1-1.5 years to construction complete
- **Cost Benefit:**Medium

### North Emergency Route (not recommended)

- **Route:**Northbound via W. 86th Lane or W. 85th Drive across the railroad tracks to Highway 72 / Coal Creek Canyon Road
- **Evacuation status change:**High - more than 1 hour reduction in overall neighborhood evacuation time
- **Requirements:**Access easements or land acquisition, complex slope grading with retaining walls, storm drainage improvements, clearance zone for entering highway, railroad approvals and permits for crossing\*, and construction variables
- **Estimated cost:**$7-15 million
- **Timeline:**5-10 years for design, railroad approvals, and construction
- **Cost Benefit:**Low

\*It is likely that the railroad could require the removal of a different crossing in Arvada in order to add this new crossing. Additionally, the City has historically experienced significant project delays due to the complex permitting and approval process with the railroad. 

### East Emergency Route (not recommended)

- **Route:**Eastbound via W. 84th Lane lines the south side of the railroad tracks to Joyce Street in Leyden Ranch East or Indiana Street
- **Evacuation status change:** Low - less than 30 minute reduction in overall neighborhood evacuation time evacuation
- **Requirements:**Access easements, potential land acquisition, and construction variables
- **Estimated cost:**$1-3 million
- **Timeline:**1-3 years to construction complete
- **Cost benefit:** Low

### Map of Alternative Routes

![Map of emergency route alternatives analyzed in Leyden neighborhood](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=7106)

This analysis looked at options to construct an alternate evacuation route for the Leyden Rock community. The west and east options are more feasible than the north option from an engineering perspective but require coordination with a variety of partner organizations including the Leyden Ranch HOA, Leyden Rock Metro District, Republic Services, and private landowners.  At this time, the Leyden Road Widening Project and the West Emergency Route are being advanced. The railroad crossing (North Emergency Route) is the most resource intensive option and is not being pursued at this time.  The East Emergency Route is also not being pursued at this time as other routes serve as better cost benefit options.
